notes:
What's new in Vekrun 0.7.11

Setup that recovers
• Fixed: a project whose setup changed a tracked file (for example `package.json`) and then set up again could stop at "Needs you" with a Docker "container name already in use" error. Setting up again now uses the steps as Vekrun repaired them in this run, redoes only what the restored files affect and leaves running services alone.
• Setup no longer writes a `packageManager` entry into `package.json` (old Node versions did this through Corepack).
• Docker Compose services get the external networks their file expects, created inside the VM, and a service Vekrun already started there is reused, never duplicated.
• The prepared VM for a project's next run is built from the repaired steps.

Coordinator spending you can see
• Scope advice and the Coordinator's other calls before Start now count on the Work Item's ledger and budget card (Planning), and are held to the Work Item's spending limit. Before, they were recorded only for the project and had no limit.
• A model you assign to the Coordinator (Settings, Factory models, Manager) is always used. With none assigned, the choice is a fixed default and no longer depends on this Mac's run history.
• The timings line shows the Coordinator's full input, cache included.

Cloudflare recipes
• Vekrun recognises Cloudflare Workers projects from their Wrangler config and sets them up in the VM with Wrangler's local mode. No Cloudflare account is used.
• Checked in the VM: Workers, D1 (migrations and constraints), KV, R2, Durable Objects (state survives a restart), Queues (retry and dead letter) and Workflows. Hyperdrive is checked against the VM's PostgreSQL. Turnstile is checked with Cloudflare's documented test keys.
• Workers AI, Vectorize, AI Gateway, AI Search and Browser Rendering are checked against local mocks of Cloudflare's documented formats and are labelled "contract mock", never verified. You add these to a project yourself.
• A Worker is previewed on Wrangler's port (8787) instead of being taken for a Node server.
• Deploying still needs your approval each time.
